newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end at highs after moderate auction results.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end at highs after moderate auction results.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Wednesday at its day high after moderately positive results in a much-awaited 10-year bond auction, traders said.
The lowest price in the auction of one trillion in 2.5 percent 10-year bonds was 100.60, about in line with expectations. The average price was 100.62.
"Demand should be moderate if not great, with no real supply concerns," a city bank trader said.
The key September closed at 125.46, up 0.33 from Tuesday's close, riding a wave of late short-covering to the day's high.
But trade was extremely thin, with turnover of only 27,172 contracts, and September spent the day pent within a 125.30 to 125.46 range.
An overnight rise in U.S. Treasury bonds helped push bonds higher during morning trade, but then the topside was capped by light profit-taking.

Some hedge selling was also detected from 125.35-40 prior to the auction on concerns that the results would be poor, the city bank trader said. Many in the market had thought demand for the bonds would be cool due to their low coupon price. The previous 197th 10-year bond had a coupon of 2.6 percent.
The 194th 10-year bond issued in April was re-opened at the auction, and some traders said this increased liquidity may have increased demand.
Relief at the auction results helped spark short-covering in late trade. The September's ability to hold its own above 125.00 since Tuesday also supported short-covering.

While some dealers said further rises may lie ahead on Thursday, others were warier, noting that Wednesday's gains were due more to a lack of strong selling interest than aggressive buying activity. "A lot of what happens depends on how institutional investors decide to move," one said.
The city bank trader said that dealers had been responsible for much of the day's activity.
Yield on the benchmark 10-year 182nd cash bond was at 2.235 percent at 0641 GMT against 2.275 percent at Tuesday's close.

East Japan Railway Co (JR East) is planning to launch two tranches of straight bonds as early as Thursday, a source at the firm said. JR East is planning to launch 40 billion yen of 12-year bonds and 30 billion yen of 20-year bonds.
Traders said that while the market was a bit concerned as to whether this fresh supply would be absorbed, it was still too early to see what impact it would have.
